html:
The second emperor of the Tang dynasty of China, born Li Shimin, who ruled from 626 to 649. Chinese historians held up his reign as a model of good government.

He helped his father, Emperor Gaozu, overthrow the Sui and found the Tang in 618. In 626 he ambushed and killed two of his brothers at the Xuanwu Gate, and his father soon handed him the throne.

As emperor he did better than his start suggests:

  • He listened to blunt advisers, above all Wei Zheng, and kept a lean, working court.
  • He crushed the Eastern Turks in 630 and took the title Heavenly Khan, opening the road to Central Asia.
  • His officials revised the Tang Code, which later shaped law in Japan, Korea and Vietnam.
  • He welcomed Xuanzang home from India in 645.

His campaigns against the Korean kingdom of Goguryeo failed. One of his concubines, Wu Zetian, later married his son and became China's only woman emperor.
